description: Human-interface hill-climb scores for Shadowroom, measured by independent reviewers from real captures of the native window and from the code at each commit. 0-5 scales unless noted; the accessibility scorecard is percent of applicable checks passed.

criteria.name: Typographic hierarchy
criteria.evidence: Type-role pass (4efa270) shipped: git grep at 72b936e finds 0 literal ui::font(n) sizes (39 at r4); every call is a role (72x LABEL, 14x MICRO, 7x TITLE, 6x BODY, 3x DISPLAY); dialog title is TITLE; one section_header() (desktop.rs:6580-6587: LABEL, MEDIUM, muted, sentence case) used by sidebar/inspector sections, theme list and Import (ingest_ui.rs:2744), so Import no longer shouts in capitals (shots/r5/import_panel__dark: 'Job', 'Destination', 'Naming'). +0.5 for consistent application. Not 4: the roles still collapse - MICRO == LABEL == 11 (layout.rs:31-33) and in Import the section header,

criteria.name: Visual novelty within identity
criteria.evidence: Round 5 adds signatures a crop identifies: the ledger now reads like an account book (picks stand above the line, rejects hang below, skipped frames notch it, a typographic '[ ]' bracket marks the strip's window); lights-out folds all chrome into that 8px line; decisions there are confirmed by a typed 13px MEDIUM mono stamp ('PICK', 'REJECT', '****') on a scrim plate - B4 as specified in spirit. All grow from mono/darkroom/keyboard and are functional. Not 5: B2 edge-code captions are still missing, so thumbnails still carry Lightroom-idiom pastel chips, and the stamp exists only in lights-out.

zed_comparison.verdict: Not yet. Whole-rubric 4.18 vs Zed 4.21 is a near-tie only because photo criteria Zed is not scored on (C5, C7 at 5) lift Shadowroom; like-for-like on Zed's 11 chrome criteria Shadowroom is 3.99 vs 4.21. Shadowroom leads on C9, C10, C14 and trails on C12 (-7 weighted points), C4 (-5), C1 (-4), C2, C11 (-3.5 each), C8, C13 (-2.5 each).

decisions.a: Agree. WCAG 1.4.11 does not require a boundary for text-labelled segments; the chosen segment's 2 px text bar on its fill (4.71-15.98:1 in all four palettes) and the focus ring (3.35-10.6:1) carry the state, and the desktop test asserts both on panel, dialog and toolbar surfaces. Residual: keycaps and Import tiles are hairlines outside the decision's wording (advisory; checkbox/text carry state).
decisions.b: Agree. Below 600 px (desktop.rs:12985) the photo keeps the filmstrip's height, a one-time hint says so, keyboard navigation is unaffected and the 16 px ledger band still jumps to any frame with shape-coded marks. Cost: thumbnails' badges leave the screen, which is exactly the 200%-scaling case (960x540 logical); Survey/Compare remain one key away.
decisions.c: Disagree from the accessibility side. Exports now never show the native chooser (chooser_for folder_picker.rs:93-110), on macOS too although the rationale names Linux. The portal FileChooser itself takes a title and current_folder (the limit is GPUI 0.2.2's prompt_for_paths), and the native dialog is the one file UI that GTK/AppKit expose to screen readers, while the built-in picker has no accessibility tree (A1). L8 regresses to fail.

Re-ran the 2,000-frame wedding cull against r5 (details in the report). Pass 1 in lights-out at 1440 gives a 1291×860 photo, a 0.5 s stamp per decision, and the playhead marching along an 8 px ledger. 'Am I done?': with 2,000 frames over about 912 px, every skipped frame either wins its 2 px bucket (empty rail) or leaves a 1 px notch. Clicking it lands within 4 frames, and Next Unreviewed finishes the job. That is a real answer at a glance,

criteria.r4_justification: r3: scrim dip on nested open fixed: modal_tint keeps one element id while any modal is open, so only the first open fades and nested surfaces fade over a steady tint (dialog.rs:263-277); tooltip shadow; text-field outlines at 3:1. r4 regressions: Preferences Appearance clipped mid-row with no scroll affordance; picker subtitle/toolbar 8px misalignment; palette description hard clip; ragged category/keycap column persists (r4/palette_empty 'Review' right edge moves with keycap width). Image menu and HC palettes are clean.

Remaining: the picker's Up button box at x=397 vs the title at 405 (r5/folder_picker; same in the 800x520 picker and the theme picker's Home button). Guide quick keys break mid-binding. decisions.a_choice_group_hairlines: Agree. Every segment is named by its text, and the state (2 px text-coloured bar on the selected fill) plus the focus ring are what convey selection and focus. dialog.rs:802-836 tests both at ≥3:1 on panel, elevated and toolbar surfaces in all four built-in palettes. Visible in r5/preferences_appearance ('Manual', 'Geist Mono', 'System' bars) and impl-r5-overlays-125/prefs_tab_motion (blue ring on 'Off'). Caveat: the test composites ghost_element.selected over the surface but does not assert that the bar is drawn. A theme that drops the bar would pass, so add a render-level check or assert the bar's colour key in the segment builder.
decisions.b_filmstrip_yields_below_600: Agree (outside this surface). At 800x520 the photo gains the filmstrip's height while the ledger band still shows position and decisions (impl-r5-loupe-800/loupe_review). Overlays are unaffected: Preferences, the palette, the picker and delete all fit at 800x520 with scroll where needed.
decisions.c_exports_use_builtin_picker_linux: Agree. Within overlays this is the more consistent choice: the built-in picker carries a verb-specific title, a subtitle, keycap hints and a primary whose verb the Ctrl+Enter hint repeats (r5/folder_picker). The GPUI 0.2.2 portal can set neither title nor start folder. Cost: no GTK bookmarks or recents. Keep a 'Use system dialog…' escape hatch if the portal gains those options.
